Grandma's Lemon Ricotta Pancakes

Prep 10 min · Cook 15 min · Serves 4

These pancakes are light, a little tangy, and they hold up beautifully under a spoonful of warm blueberry compote. I've been making them every Sunday since my kids were small, and the trick is folding the whipped egg whites in at the very end.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup whole-milk ricotta
  • 3 eggs, separated
  • 3/4 cup milk
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • zest of 2 lemons
  • pinch of salt
  • butter for the pan

Method

  1. Whisk the ricotta, egg yolks, milk and lemon zest until smooth.
  2. In another bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir into the wet mix until just combined.
  3. Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them in gently in two additions.
  4. Heat a skillet over medium-low heat, add a little butter, and cook 1/4 cup portions for about 2 minutes per side.

Notes

The batter keeps in the fridge for a day, but the pancakes will be a little flatter. Swap the lemon for orange zest in winter. If you don't have ricotta, a thick strained yogurt works in a pinch, though the texture is denser.
